claim: Instruction-tuned LLMs asked to pick a number 'completely at random' between 1 and 10 produce highly non-uniform outputs: output entropy is 1.07-1.88 nats vs 2.30 for uniform (Llama-2-13B-chat heavily favors 5), and similar collapse occurs for random names (Mistral-7B-Instruct picks 'Avery' ~40x more than U.S. base rates).

paper.title: Forcing Diffuse Distributions out of Language Models
paper.venue: COLM 2024 (per common listing; not verified in text)
paper.citation_source: paperclip CLI search index (`paperclip search -s arxiv`), output saved in sources/paperclip_counts_final.txt; Semantic Scholar Graph API returned HTTP 429 on every attempt 2026-09-29 (shared rate limit)
paper.s2_batch_record_title: Forcing Diffuse Distributions out of Language Models

experiment.location_in_paper: Sec 2 (metrics: KL, entropy, coverage), Sec 4.1 (baseline failure), Fig 1, Table 1; App (fine-tuning details)
experiment.task_or_benchmark: RNG: 'Generate a random number between 1 and 10. Output only the number between two curly braces, like this: {number}. Don't output code.'; BABYNAMES: random English first name.
experiment.intervention_or_prompts: Prompts above; full random sampling (T=1); then the paper's LoRA distribution-matching fine-tune (not part of claim).
experiment.evaluation_procedure: Exact output probabilities over valid targets / 1,000 samples; entropy and Coverage-1000 vs natural (uniform) distribution.
experiment.main_comparison: Baseline (untuned) model distribution vs uniform/natural distribution.
experiment.main_result: RNG entropy: Gemma 1.16, Llama-2 1.07, Mistral 1.88 vs 2.30 uniform; coverage 8-10/10. BABYNAMES entropy 3.19-4.02 vs 6.43 natural; coverage 129-225 unique names vs 714. Baseline models would need T>10 to match tuned-model entropy.

reproducibility.missing: Trivial to re-run on any model (prompt given verbatim). Mistral-7B-instruct minor version unspecified in paper. Did not open README/code files beyond tree listing.

downstream.title: Base Models Beat Aligned Models at Randomness and Creativity
downstream.summary: Read abstract and Sec 2.2: Llama-3.1 base vs Llama-Instruct and Tulu SFT/DPO/full on uniform integers 0-10; aligned models strongly prefer '7' with chi^2 divergence ~an order of magnitude above base; aligned models avoid repeats in sequences.

downstream.title: Instruction-Tuned Language Models Cannot Sample from Distributions They Can Describe
downstream.summary: Read abstract and Sec 3.3: gpt-4o at T=1 picks 42 in 78% of 'uniform 1-100' calls, 7 in 97% of 1-10 calls, 'heads' 85%; five other instruction-tuned families show the same favored values; instruct models worse than bases.

downstream.title: Verbalized Sampling (App G.5 dice roll)
downstream.summary: Read G.5: direct prompting to roll a die collapses (e.g., Gemini-2.5-Pro mostly '4'; mean KL 0.926 vs uniform); sequence/VS prompting near-uniform (KL ~0.06).

downstream.title: How Random is Random? Evaluating the Randomness and Humaness of LLMs' Coin Flips
downstream.summary: Abstract/intro read: in binary random-sequence generation, GPT-4 and Llama 3 exhibit and exacerbate nearly every human randomness bias tested, while GPT-3.5 behaves more randomly - bias is model-dependent, not monotone in capability.

downstream_summary: Strongly replicated: 2025-26 work shows GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Pro and multiple open families collapse on single random draws, with post-training making it worse than base models; asking for sequences or verbalized distributions largely fixes it.
